# Yomi RSS Reader

Formerly KiJi. In short: Yomi Reader.

Yomi Reader is a modern, performant RSS reader built to stay open for weeks or months: light on memory and CPU, with fixed cache limits, a virtualized article list, small refresh batches that pause during sleep, and automatic log cleanup, so memory does not keep growing. Stations, Defuddle/Readability extraction, Markdown sync for saved articles.

Yomi Reader is free and open source, and runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux as native Tauri builds (x64, and ARM64 where supported). Tagline: "A modern, performant RSS reader."

Brand summary:

- Built to stay open — runs for weeks or months without slowing down; caches have fixed limits, the list renders only what is on screen, refresh runs a few feeds at a time and pauses during sleep, and logs older than two days are deleted.
- Local-only — no account, no server; all data is stored in a local SQLite database.
- Stations — feeds grouped by tags; views switch between unread and saved; no algorithmic timeline.
- Reader mode — Defuddle and Readability extraction engines convert full page HTML into clean article text.
- Markdown sync — saved articles are written to a local folder as Markdown files.
- Reader themes — 13 book-style themes (Paper, Sepia, Calm, Eye Care, Washi, Parchment, Newsprint, E-Ink, Solarized, Quiet, Midnight, OLED Night, High Contrast), each with a light and a dark version.
- Assistant access (MCP) — Claude Desktop (one-click extension), Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code (install links), Codex, and any MCP app can read what the user shares: the article open in Yomi Reader, stations, feeds, articles by time range, search, a digest, and saved articles with highlights. Optional changes (mark read, star, save) only behind a separate "Allow assistants to make changes" switch. Off by default, runs on the user's computer through the local `kiji-app --mcp` server; set up in Settings → Assistant.
